engines.name: Merlin · Sea Level
engines.description: Reusable kerosene engine used in nine-engine Falcon 9 booster clusters.
engines.notes: SpaceX publishes 845 kN sea-level thrust per engine and a 57% minimum throttle in its May 2025 payload guide. Isp and vacuum thrust must be supplied as model inputs. One ignition is a conservative mission setting, not the engine reuse limit.

engines.name: Merlin · Vacuum
engines.description: Vacuum-optimized Merlin variant used to insert payloads and perform upper-stage maneuvers.
engines.notes: SpaceX publishes 981 kN vacuum thrust and a 63.8% minimum throttle in its May 2025 payload guide. Isp must be supplied as a model input. Two burns is a conservative mission setting, not a published maximum restart count.

engines.name: BE-4
engines.description: Methane-fueled booster engine powering both New Glenn and Vulcan.
engines.notes: Current manufacturer thrust reference: 2,846 kN, throttling to 978 kN. The page does not publish Isp or vacuum thrust. Rating is a family reference, not a certified Vulcan or New Glenn configuration.

engines.name: BE-3U
engines.description: Restartable hydrogen upper-stage engine supporting orbital insertion and transfer missions.
engines.notes: Manufacturer reference is 890 kN with throttling to 445 kN. Isp is not published on this page. Two burns is a conservative mission setting; this is not a published maximum restart count.

engines.name: Rutherford · Sea Level
engines.description: Compact electrically pumped engine used in Electron's nine-engine first stage.
engines.notes: The Electron page publishes 190 kN total liftoff thrust for nine engines and a first-stage Isp of 311 s without an explicit pressure condition. This Isp is displayed for context, not fixed as vacuum Isp. Enter vacuum thrust and Isp as model inputs. Battery and power-system mass belong in stage dry mass.

engines.name: Rutherford · Vacuum
engines.description: Electron's vacuum-optimized second-stage engine for small-payload orbital insertion.
engines.notes: The published second-stage rating is 25.8 kN and 343 s. Restart and throttle limits are not published here; the preset conservatively uses one burn and fixed throttle. Battery and power-system mass belong in stage dry mass.

engines.name: Vinci
engines.description: Cryogenic upper-stage engine with multiple ignitions for orbital insertion and transfer maneuvers.
engines.notes: ESA publishes 180 kN and up to four ignitions. Isp and continuous throttle limits are not published on this reference page; enter model values. APU, tanks and supporting systems must be included in stage dry mass.

engines.name: Vulcain 2.1
engines.description: Hydrogen core-stage engine used with solid boosters on Ariane 6.
engines.notes: Vacuum rating is 1,370 kN. Isp and continuous throttle limits are not published on this page. Ariane 6 also uses strap-on boosters, which this serial two-stage layout does not model.
